claim_en: ha-adam ('the man') carries exactly the letters of adamah ('earth') — 'for he was created from the earth'; the Kitzur adds the word itself abbreviates ash, blood, bile (the body's stuff). Letter-multiset verified.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:27 (the Soferim classification)
claim_en: be-tzelem Elohim ('in the image of God') — MS rules the Name here HOLY. The holy/profane classification layer is uninstrumented in SNAPSHOT — filed to the classification gap (station 13).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 1:28 (Yevamot 65b; Tanchuma Noach; Bereshit Rabbah 8)
claim_en: ve-khivshuha ('and subdue it') is written LEAN — no vav after the shin, so the skeleton reads 'and subdue HER' in the singular: Yevamot's derivation that the man, not the woman, is commanded to conquer. The skeleton stands three times in the Torah — here, and twice as the EWE-LAMB of the leper's and the Nazirite's offerings (a new skeleton-collision member).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 1:28 (the Masorah)
claim_en: u-redu ('and have dominion') — the Kitzur's Masorah pair: here, and 'go down to Gat of the Philistines' (Amos 6:2, outside the Torah instrument): merit rules even the fish; sin goes down to Gat. In the Torah the imperative form stands ONCE — and the same skeleton returns re-pointed in the curses (ve-radu, 'your foes shall rule over you', Lev 26:17): the Torah's own inner echo of the threat.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 1:29 (the Masorah)
claim_en: peri etz ('fruit of a tree') — the Kitzur's Masorah pair, station 1: 'that has within it the fruit of a tree' (here, the pe soft after 'within it').

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 1:29 (the Masorah)
claim_en: Station 2 completes the pair: peri etz hadar ('fruit of a beautiful tree', Lev 23:40) — the hint that the tree Adam ate from was the ETROG. Both stations Torah-side; the pair is EXACT (no third adjacency in the stream).

MS's rule: 'every kol bound to the next word takes qamatz (the long a); every kol carrying its own accent takes holam (the o-dot)' — the verse's first two u-le-khol ('and to every') are bound, and both written with qamatz.
The rule's other half in the SAME verse: the third u-le-khol carries its own accent (the upright conjunctive stroke) — and takes the holam, exactly as ruled.
yereq ('green herb') — MS: 'with SIX dots': two segols (the three-dot e) — six points on the one word, counted in-stream.
yom ha-shishi ('the sixth day') closing creation's ledger: initials yod-he — first half of the four-letter Name with which the work of creation was sealed.
va-yekhulu ha-shamayim ('and the heavens were finished') opens the next verse with vav-he — the Name's second half: the seal runs across the day-six/day-seven seam.
